headline: EV batteries hold charge better than expected
standfirst: A new study reveals electric vehicle batteries last longer than many drivers feared.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: A new study shows used EV batteries keep 90% of their capacity after 150,000 km.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Many drivers worried about rapid battery degradation in electric cars over time.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This data suggests EVs have a longer usable lifespan than previously assumed.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future reports on long term battery health as more EVs hit high mileage.

caption:
A new study shows electric vehicle batteries retain 90 percent of their capacity after 150,000 kilometers.

Range anxiety often focuses on how far a car goes on a single charge. However, battery degradation is the hidden concern for second-hand buyers. This data from Ars Technica offers a clearer picture of how these batteries hold up over the long haul.

Does knowing this make you more likely to consider buying a used electric car?
